key_insight: A spatially grounded Concept Bottleneck Model uses coarse lesion regions to make breast ultrasound predictions more anatomically plausible and concept evidence more trustworthy.
clinical_relevance: This approach may improve the reliability and interpretability of ultrasound-assisted breast diagnosis by aligning model explanations with lesion morphology and posterior acoustic features.
method: Derive two weakly supervised zones from each lesion mask: an in-lesion region for morphology concepts and a posterior acoustic band for posterior phenomena.
Train concept maps with a grouped spatial grounding objective to encourage concept evidence in the right anatomy.
Use a linear bottleneck classifier to preserve semantic faithfulness in the final diagnosis.
evidence_signal: Across five-fold stratified group cross-validation, the model improved diagnostic AUROC and concept macro-AUROC while substantially increasing spatial alignment; a Train-corrupt/Test-clean test further assessed the effect of annotation quality.
watch_item: Performance and explanation quality depend on the availability and accuracy of coarse lesion supervision, so weak or inconsistent annotations could limit real-world reliability.
paper_title: Spatially Grounded Concept Bottleneck Models for Trustworthy Breast Ultrasound Diagnosis
